ordered_diagnoses: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder

s1.syndrome_frame: Hematuria and dysuria with a bladder lesion
salient_findings: Focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
Heterogeneous enhancement of the lesion on CT
key_facts: Past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy
Urinalysis showed 6–8 red blood cells and 4–6 pus cells per high-power field
Ultrasound showed a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder
CT showed a well-defined soft-tissue–density lesion with calcific specks in the bladder
Lesion demonstrated heterogeneous enhancement on CT
Right calyceal calculus with mild pelvicalyceal dilatation

shortlist: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder

shortlist.label: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Most common type of bladder cancer, consistent with imaging findings

shortlist.label: Urothelial carcinoma with squamous differentiation
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the presence of a polypoidal lesion and hematuria

shortlist.label: Papillary urothelial carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Common subtype of bladder cancer, consistent with the polypoidal appearance on imaging

shortlist.label: Bladder endometriosis
shortlist.why_kept: Possible given the patient's history of abdominal hysterectomy and the presence of a cystic area in the left adnexa

shortlist.label: Malacoplakia of the bladder
shortlist.why_kept: Rare condition that can cause a polypoidal lesion and hematuria, consistent with some of the imaging findings

raw.rationale: The presence of a focal hypoechoic polypoidal lesion in the bladder on ultrasound and a well-defined soft-tissue-density lesion with calcific specks on CT, demonstrating heterogeneous enhancement, is most consistent with a neoplastic process such as papillary urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Transitional cell carcinoma of the bladder
rejected.why: While possible, the specific characteristics of the lesion are more suggestive of papillary urothelial carcinoma.

rejected.label: Urothelial carcinoma with squamous differentiation
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence provided to suggest squamous differentiation.

rejected.label: Bladder endometriosis
rejected.why: The patient's past medical history of abdominal hysterectomy and the imaging findings do not strongly support endometriosis as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Malacoplakia of the bladder
rejected.why: Malacoplakia typically presents with more diffuse bladder wall thickening and does not usually appear as a well-defined polypoidal lesion.
